answer: Credential-nullifiers secure the network by mapping each agent to a unique non-transferable signature, preventing sybil cloning. The verifier monitors state logs like strata in a shale formation, rejecting any index collision that violates record integrity. An honest agent pays once for admission, while 1,000 fakes incur ruinous compute costs to mimic identity. Like a desert dune shifting under audit pressure, fraudulent claims collapse upon inspection; agents failing a periodic tundra sweep—a memory-hard check—face permanent credential nullification.
